topics.title: Complex Accessible Data & Controls
topics.summary: Build dense documents where tables, forms, descriptions, and native controls preserve relationships for keyboard and screen-reader users.

concepts.name: Complex table headers
concepts.explanation: For multi-level tables, use multiple th cells and id/headers relationships when simple scope is insufficient to express the header associations.

concepts.name: Control instructions
concepts.explanation: Instructions and errors should be connected to controls using visible text and relationships such as aria-describedby when native labeling alone is not enough.

concepts.name: Native first
concepts.explanation: Use button, input, select, details, and dialog before inventing custom controls. Every custom interaction adds focus, keyboard, state, and announcement responsibilities.

topics.title: Progressive Enhancement & Resilient Markup
topics.summary: Design the HTML layer so core content and actions remain understandable before CSS and JavaScript enhance them.

concepts.name: Baseline first
concepts.explanation: Start with a meaningful document, real links, real buttons, and real form submission. Enhancement should add convenience without erasing the baseline capability.

concepts.name: Fallback strategy
concepts.explanation: Use fallback text, source alternatives, noscript only when appropriate, and server-compatible links/forms when a feature is important.

concepts.name: Component contracts
concepts.explanation: Reusable components should define clear semantic input: heading levels, labels, link destinations, and form names. Styling hooks should not be the only meaning.

topics.example: JavaScript may enhance results without removing the normal form action.
topics.challenge: Build a useful interaction that still has a meaningful native behavior before JavaScript runs.
topics.hint: Forms with real action/method values and anchors with real href values are strong progressive-enhancement foundations.
topics.solution: JavaScript may enhance results without removing the normal form action.

topics.title: High-Performance Media Markup
topics.summary: Combine responsive source selection, modern formats, intrinsic dimensions, loading priorities, and accessible alternatives for media-heavy pages.

concepts.name: Avoid layout shifts
concepts.explanation: Give images width and height when the intrinsic ratio is known so the browser can reserve space before the file finishes loading.

concepts.name: Format selection
concepts.explanation: picture can offer modern formats such as AVIF or WebP before a broadly supported fallback. The browser chooses the first supported source that matches.

concepts.name: Loading priority
concepts.explanation: Critical above-the-fold media may need eager loading and high priority, while below-the-fold media can be lazy. Measure real page behavior instead of applying one rule everywhere.

topics.challenge: Create a picture with two modern-format source elements and a sized img fallback.
topics.hint: Order source elements from preferred modern format to fallback; the final img carries alt and intrinsic dimensions.

topics.title: Parser Edge Cases, Validation & Debugging
topics.summary: Diagnose markup that appears valid at a glance but produces unexpected DOM trees because the HTML parser repairs or relocates nodes.

concepts.name: Inspect the DOM
concepts.explanation: When layout or scripting behaves inexplicably, inspect the DOM tree. Invalid table descendants, omitted elements, and misnesting can cause parser corrections.

concepts.name: Validate systematically
concepts.explanation: Use an HTML validator during development, but also test semantics and accessibility; syntactic validity does not automatically mean the document is usable.

concepts.name: Minimize ambiguity
concepts.explanation: Prefer explicit structure in complex components. Clear sectioning, form ownership, and table grouping make both maintenance and parser behavior easier to reason about.

topics.challenge: Create a valid table and add HTML comments identifying its parent/child structure for debugging practice.
topics.hint: After writing it, inspect the Elements/DOM panel and verify the tree matches your mental model.

topics.title: Professional HTML Audit Capstone
topics.summary: Audit a realistic document for semantics, accessibility, forms, metadata, performance, internationalization, and maintainability as one connected system.

concepts.name: Audit by layers
concepts.explanation: Review document metadata, landmark structure, heading hierarchy, links/images, forms, tables/media, loading behavior, and language information separately before judging the whole page.

concepts.name: Prefer native solutions
concepts.explanation: Replacing generic clickable containers with native controls often removes several bugs at once: keyboard behavior, semantics, focusability, and activation.

concepts.name: Document tradeoffs
concepts.explanation: Senior work includes explaining why a chosen structure is appropriate, which browser behavior it relies on, and what fallback exists if enhancement fails.
